correctness.rationale: The dyadic uniformity and exact Markov excursion reduction are proved, with an explicit first-step geometric mixture. Ballot and defect formulas handle both drift signs. originality.rationale: The theorem is the explicit joint near-critical first-return scaling for the original closed Pelikan random map with initial normalized upper band, distinguished from critical occupation laws and from fixed-parameter resetting/absorbing statistics. Closest primary full texts Hata–Yano 2021, Yan et al. 2023 and Monthus 2024 were materially compared; none states the triangular-array crossover. Existing exact transforms are acknowledged rather than presented as novel. Search results did not locate equivalent coverage. Priority risk: a stronger general near-critical lattice hitting theorem may imply this model-specific statement.
residual_risks: Classical Brownian-with-drift first-passage scaling has analogous formulas; possible unindexed all-parameter theorem subsumes the map-specific return observable.
Monthus supplies related exact transforms; a general published uniform asymptotic result not identified in the inspected full text could cover the new scaling.
Brevitt–Klages 2026 on an open Pelikan variant was available only as a title and abstract, not full text; its setting differs but historical priority remains to be assessed independently.

value.rationale: The first-return survival of the upper dyadic band is a natural quantitative recurrence observable at the Pelikan map transition, where zero-bias behavior changes to a nonzero permanent-escape probability. The nontrivial parameter-window profile includes negative-bias escape and the positive-bias decaying side in one exact formula, adding finite-horizon information not supplied by fixed-parameter recurrence laws. Its specificity is motivated by the original model and parameter scale, not by an arbitrary numerical slice.
